atoms.text: “I am not sure what it is,” said Coto, “but I have an idea how we can see it more clearly. My mum showed me how to make casts of imprints in the dirt.” Coto went to their shed and grabbed everything they would need to make the plaster. Luckily his parents used this stuff in their own work!

My mum showed me how to make casts of imprints in the dirt.”</voice> <break time='500ms'/> Kohtoh went to their shed and grabbed everything they would need to make the plaster. Luckily his parents used this stuff in their own work!

hint.text:
The plaster that Coto is talking about is “plaster of Paris.” It can be mixed with water to create a thick mixture.

To make a cast, you take the mixed plaster and pour it straight onto the print. The plaster dries very quickly and can be picked up after waiting for about an hour.

The dirt can then be cleaned off the bottom, and the print can be seen clearly in the hardened plaster mould.

atoms.text:
Twenty minutes later, they were pouring the mixture into the print. “Ok, now we have to wait for the plaster to dry a bit. We only have to wait a few hours,” explained Coto.
“A few hours! That’s too long. What if the animal is already moving to the next town?” said Estefania nervously.
“It will work, trust me!” Coto said. A few hours later, they pulled the dried plaster from the ground and brushed off the dirt.

atoms.sound: Why did Kohtoh know how to make a cast of an imprint?

atoms.a: Choose the statement that correctly contrasts Coto’s and Estefania’s responses to the drying time for the plaster.
atoms.sound: Choose the statement that correctly contrasts Kohtoh’s and Estefania’s responses to the drying time for the plaster.
atoms.hint: When we contrast, we find what makes two or more things different.
b: Coto was annoyed they had to wait for the plaster to dry for so long, but Estefania did not mind.
++Estefania was nervous they would lose track of the animal, but Coto thought it would be okay.

atoms.text: “It’s a big dog!” exclaimed Estefania. “Look, you can see big nails and four large toes,” she said pointing to parts of the print.

atoms.text:
“I guess he would have been large enough to lean in through your window and take the shawl off your bed!” Coto was very excited. They were close to solving the mystery, he could feel it!
“Now we need to find the dog,” said Estefania.

atoms.text: They looked at each other and smiled. There was only one dog in the small village who could possibly have made the print - Grandita!
atoms.sound: ssml: They looked at each other and smiled. There was only one dog in the small village who could possibly have made the print <break time='500ms'/>Grandeta!

atoms.a: Who identified the animal from the imprint first?
Choose the statement that correctly compares Coto’s and Estefania’s responses to the print.
atoms.sound: Choose the statement that correctly compares Kohtoh’s and Estefania’s responses to the print.
atoms.hint: When we compare, we find how two or more things are similar.
b: ++They smiled and thought of the same dog.
They thought the print belonged to different dogs.

atoms.text: Together, they located Grandita’s home. “It’s there! My shawl is there!” yelled Estefania with joy. “Look, she was sleeping on it.” The shawl was quite dirty, but Estefania said, “We can wash it, and it will be just like before. My grandma made it very tough.” The mystery was solved, but Coto’s love for detective work was just beginning!

atoms.a: Choose the statement that correctly contrasts Coto’s goal from the beginning of the story to his goal at the end.
atoms.sound: Choose the statement that correctly contrasts Kohtoh’s goal from the beginning of the story to his goal at the end.
atoms.hint: When we contrast, we find what makes two or more things different.
b: At the beginning, Coto didn’t want to help Estefania. By the end, Coto was frustrated that they had the shawl, but it was destroyed.
++At the beginning, Coto wanted to help his friend. By the end, Coto decided to become a detective.

atoms.a: Choose the statement that correctly contrasts Estefania’s feelings from the beginning of the story to her feelings at the end.
atoms.hint: When we contrast, we find what makes two or more things different.
b: ++At the beginnng, Estefania was very sad about losing her shawl. By the end, Estefania was happy and glad to have solved the mystery.
At the beginning, Estefania was excited to solve the mystery. By the end, she was happy she met Coto.
